issue_context.title: e2e conformance pod sending total tests back as zero for conformance image 1.25.x
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Our team uses sonobuoy to run the conformormance tests on a cluster and displays the results to the users.
We have been using conformance image 1.21.x until now and it sends back progress data to sonobuoy pod and our service reads it from the sonobuoy pod.
The progress data included the total number of tests to be run and the completed tests. For 1.21 conformance we were receiving this data properly but when switching to 1.25.x conformance we are getting the total tests as zero. This is causing issues in our UI.
Not sure what version of conformance image introduced this but we were using 1.21 and started seeing this issue after moving to 1.25.x. The conformance image versions in between 1.21 -1.25 are not CVE free so we cannot use them.

### What did you expect to happen?

Total number of tests should be non-zero for conformance image 1.25.x. Ideally i think it should come back as 360.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- provision a 1.25 kubernetes kind (or anything else) cluster
- Install sonobuoy 
- Run conformance scan on the cluster
- Check the annotation on the sonobuoy pod ` sonobuoy.hept.io/status` . This is set by sonobuoy based on the data it gets back from the e2e conformance pod.
- The total tests comes as zero

### Anything else we need to know?

I just found it on 1.25.x conformance. Not really sure when this was introduced. Need to make sure back dated versiosn also have this fix in case they have this issue.

### Kubernetes version

<details>
1.25 cluster with 1.25.x conformance with any sonobuoy version
```console
$ kubectl version
# paste output here
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>
ANY
</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# paste output here
$ uname -a
# paste output here

# On Windows:
C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture
# paste output here
```

</details>


### Install tools

<details>

</details>

<details>

</details>


### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

<details>
Conformacne e2e plugin
</details>

yeah, well, it seems I phrased it wrong , but you answer my question

Thanks
The reporter used to have the side effect of writing JSON messages to stdout. But I removed that in 1.26.

Now it is as @chendave said, mostly the presence of this reporter can be ignored during normal test runs.

I have asked a few times whether sonobuoy uses this report when running tests in parallel, but so far we have only been able to determine that sonobuoy supports parallel testing. It remains unclear to me whether that is getting used.

My suspicion is that this report is going to be broken when running tests in parallel because each process is going to report its own, local process to the remote URL, with no way of consolidating the different (and conflicting) reports.

We can't fix this, but perhaps you can check and document this as a known limitation?

I don't think that this is a regression, because I don't see how this could have worked differently before with Ginkgo v1, but I am not sure. This could be similar to how I am testing output handling (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/framework/log_test.go), except that the unit test needs to be in a separate directory similar to the [cleanup test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/e2e/framework/internal/unittests/cleanup) because defining the Ginkgo test suite is global.

I will take an investigation with regarding to the unittest but I think it's only nice to have as long as this PR fixed that issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114313
Let me prepare a unit test with some TODOs - shouldn't take long, I know that code.
> completed is the number of completed tests in that worker, not in the suite

seems like it is calculated as this from `Test Suite completed`, total is 5.
proc1:  1 completed (passed)
proc2:  1 completed (passed), 1 failed
proc3:   2 failed 
this matches with the total test that are executed. 

`total` is not set correctly though, only proc3 has the value set but it's for the entire suite. 
See https://github.com/chendave/kubernetes/pull/2
It cannot run Ginkgo tests in parallel, though.
for what it's worth - the behavior y'all are noticing isn't a regression.  it was always broken when running in parallel.  options to fix would include:
